bc_the_grooves.blurb: The Grooves is a compact wall within the Fortress sector at Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton in the Okanagan. It holds 13 routes, mostly bolted single-pitch lines plus a pair of trad climbs. The grade spread leans toward the middle and upper range: about seven climbs sit in the 5.10 band, four in 5.11, and one each in the 5.8 and 5.9 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper face and groove terrain more than true beginners. The Fortress as a whole is among the busiest parts of Skaha, so expect company on good weekends.

bc_juniper_point.blurb: Juniper Point is a horseshoe-shaped cliff right at the water's edge in Lighthouse Park, on the North Shore near Vancouver. Of its 13 routes, ten are top-rope problems with fixed anchors above, and three are trad lines. Grades run from easy 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, making it a handy place to introduce newer climbers to outdoor rock while still offering a few harder tests. Trails reach the base from either end of the wall, and the walk from the parking lot is short. Bring a helmet and a rope long enough to reach the top anchors.

bc_after_work.blurb: After Work is a small sport crag on the Cheekye River just north of Squamish, in the Sea to Sky corridor, sitting beside its neighbour After Party. All 13 routes are bolted. Grades start around 5.6, then cluster in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a single 5.12 at the top end, so there is plenty for intermediate climbers and a little for those wanting a challenge. The crag is fairly new and has the feel of a quick evening stop rather than a full-day destination. Check recent conditions on the river before heading in, since the walk-in has changed over the years.

bc_polished_wall.blurb: Polished Wall is a west-facing crag in the Kinnaird Bluffs above Castlegar, in the West Kootenays. It carries 13 routes: nine sport lines and four trad, a few of them two pitches long, and every route is equipped with fixed anchors. Grades span a friendly range, from 5.7 through 5.11, with the greatest numbers at 5.7, 5.8 and 5.10, so it works well for moderate climbers building toward harder terrain. To get there, follow the trail up and left past Open Book Wall. Being west-facing, it gets its sun later in the day.

bc_wapiti_wall.blurb: Wapiti Wall is a small cluster of cliff faces beside the highway along Arrow Lake, in the Castlegar area of the West Kootenays. It has 13 routes, split between sport and trad, with grades mostly from 5.9 into the 5.11 range and a few harder lines above that. The wall has an easy, close-to-the-car approach with a good variety of moderate and fun climbing. Because it sits so near the road, it makes a convenient quick stop, though climbers should stay aware of traffic. The cliffs around the lake are described as sunny, which makes it a reasonable spring choice.
